pf.license.need: No state license to perform a wedding in most places. Many states ask an officiant to hold a credential: an ordination, a registration with the county, or a state officiant's card. The state's form says which applies; the business says what it holds.
pf.license.who holds it: Each officiant holds their own credential where the state asks for one. The business holds any business license or registration. Ceremonies at a venue follow the venue's own rules.
what to ask: The officiant's credential, where the state's form asks for one (the business writes it in its own words)
The business license or registration number, where the city or county asks for one
The liability insurance policy and its end date, if a venue asks
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a credential, license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a credential (D96): the business and each officiant go live once set up and the owner says yes; a ceremony the owner says needs a credential they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.signing the papers: The marriage paperwork is the couple's and the county's. The officiant signs only what the state's form asks for. Rosie never files or signs any paper.
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a credential the owner says has lapsed pauses that officiant's ceremonies until the owner says it's renewed (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance on file, with its end date, where a venue asks. Many venues ask for a certificate naming them.
pf.license.background checks: Only where a venue or the state's form asks. The business's own word, never checked by Rosie.
pf.license.the age to marry: Rosie never books a ceremony where anyone is under the state's age to marry (see pf.safety).

pf.questions.flags: A health note or an access need is flagged on the secure page: the officiant calls (never a text) and plans the spot and the length to fit.
pf.questions.who may book: An adult. Either partner may book, and both sign the ceremony agreement. Anyone booking for someone else says they have that person's yes. Nobody under the state's age to marry may be booked.

stops the booking.words: Someone says they are being made to marry, or is scared to say no
stops the booking.says: If you are in danger now, call 911. No ceremony is booked here.
stops the booking.booking: No booking. The owner gets a plain note that a booking was stopped for safety, with no names or details.

stops the booking.words: Someone under the state's age to marry is named as one of the couple
stops the booking.says: A ceremony can't go ahead for anyone under the state's age to marry.
stops the booking.booking: No booking, and the owner is told in plain words, with no names.

stops the booking.words: Someone can't say what they want, or says they didn't agree
stops the booking.says: The officiant can't go ahead until each person says yes in their own words.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until each person has answered for themselves.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: Someone at the ceremony faints, or can't breathe, or has a health emergency
safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: Call 911 now if it's serious. The ceremony stops, and help comes first.
safety steps, then the booking goes on.booking: The ceremony stops; the owner is told. The owner decides what's kept; Rosie makes no new charge.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: Fire, smoke or a gas smell at the venue on the day
safety steps, then the booking goes on.booking: The ceremony moves or stops; the owner decides with the couple.

pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Rosie never judges a situation: the officiant or the owner decides.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code, given to the officiant at arrival by the couple, or by a day-of contact named on the booking.
pf.visit.check-in at the studio: The code at the desk, or the officiant types it.
pf.visit.setup: The officiant arrives 30 minutes before the start, checks the spot and the sound, and has the ceremony form and the signing papers ready.
pf.visit.the ceremony: The script follows the ceremony form. A change after the form is final needs both partners' yes, given in person or in writing before the day.
pf.visit.the schedule: The start time is the couple's. A late arrival shortens the set-up, never the ceremony.
pf.visit.work changes on the day: Extra time or an extra reading added on the day only with both partners' written yes, at the rate shown before booking, paid at the visit or on the bill (D91).
pf.visit.proof it's done: The officiant texts DONE when the ceremony is over and the signed papers are with the couple or the county's office.
pf.visit.props: Nothing is handed over or sold at the ceremony. Any printed program or card is the couple's own.

pf.money.travel: Free within 25 miles; $40 from 25 to 50 miles; farther, quoted first.
pf.money.early start: Not offered: the officiant arrives 30 minutes before the start, at no charge.
pf.money.tax: No tax line unless the owner sets a rate where the state taxes the service.

pf.messages.never in a text: Health, access and family notes, the venue's codes, any minor's name, and anything about a ceremony that could hurt someone stay on the secure page and the officiant's job link, never in a text to the couple, the owner or the staff. A text says only 'a note is on the page'.
pf.messages.photos: Photos of the ceremony go only with each person's own yes; a parent's for anyone under 18.
pf.messages.minors: A ring bearer or flower child under 18 is named only on the secure page; a parent's yes, and the parent stays. Rosie never texts a minor first.

pf.staff.licenses: Each officiant's credential where the state asks for one, as the business says it; nothing is looked up.
pf.staff.away from the studio: Ceremonies at venues, homes and parks are the usual work; the venue's rules and the state's form apply.
pf.staff.supervision: A new officiant works with a lead officiant the owner names, where the state's rules allow.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs every custom quote, any stand-in officiant and any extra time added on the day.
pf.staff.stand-ins: On location: another officiant the couple accepts, offered by name; the agreement names the stand-in, so with no reply by 8pm the evening before, the stand-in comes and the owner calls. A full refund is always the other choice. The stand-in gets the ceremony form and the venue's rules, nothing else.

pf.rules.license shown: A credential or license number on the confirmation or the receipt only where the state's form asks for one (a switch from the state form).
pf.rules.away from the studio: Ceremonies at homes, parks and venues are normal work; the venue's own rules apply.
pf.rules.written contract: The business's own ceremony agreement, signed by the couple and the business before money is taken; any parts the state adds come from the state form.
pf.rules.date hold: A ceremony date stays saved while the agreement is signed: up to 48 hours (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.cancel and date change: Free to cancel until 24 hours before; after that, what the agreement says, with the owner's OK. One free date change to an open date (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.final count: The guest count is set on the ceremony form, due 7 days before.
pf.rules.minors: A parent's yes for anyone under 18 named in the ceremony, and the parent stays.
pf.rules.photo use: Photos only with each person's own yes; a parent's for anyone under 18. No answer means no.
pf.rules.weather: An outdoor ceremony has a rain plan. The owner sets a weather limit (the example: heavy rain or storms in the forecast); over it, the owner is asked the afternoon before to keep it under the rain plan or move it.
pf.rules.records: Agreements, ceremony forms and payments kept 7 years, or longer where the state asks.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for ceremonies:
ceremony: The start time can't move: a late officiant shortens the set-up, never the ceremony
A person asks to stop or hesitates: the ceremony pauses, and each person answers for themselves
A health problem during the ceremony: help comes first, then the owner decides
The officiant can't come: a stand-in the agreement names, or a full refund
The couple moves the date: one free move, if the officiant is free that day
The ceremony moves to another place on the day: the travel fee is checked again before anyone agrees
Rain on an outdoor ceremony: the rain plan, called the afternoon before
Someone added late (a reading, a guest speaker): only with the couple's yes and the owner's OK
The marriage papers aren't ready: that's the couple's job with the county; the officiant signs nothing that isn't ready
A booking for someone under the state's age to marry: stopped, and the owner is told in plain words

notes: Built Tue Oct 27 2026 (batch E2, new) from the refitted planner overlay (Event), copied and changed: the plug-in is written for officiating (weddings at a venue, a studio room, elopements, custom ceremonies, rehearsals), not planning. Facts: contracts (the ceremony agreement), documents, firststeps (the planning call, the ceremony form), forms (the ceremony form), extrawork (extra time on the day), video (vow sessions by video), weather (an outdoor ceremony), photos (the custom quote). No switches: standin is not on, since the officiant named in a booking is never swapped without the couple's choice (the stand-in words are in pf.staff). License: the officiant's credential and the business license are the business's own word, nothing looked up (D96); the master's license steps stay as the sibling set them (S1-60 and S2-28 off). Money: A list|deposit|counter (studio ceremony $250, $50 deposit, $200 at the studio), list|card|counter (meeting $150, card for the $25 fee), list|none|none (free first call), list|full|none (vow session $150), photos|deposit|bill (custom ceremony $600, $150 deposit, $450 on the bill). B list|deposit|card (venue ceremony $450, $150 deposit, $300 at DONE), list|full|none (elopement $300 paid in full), list|none|bill (rehearsal $150, bill after), photos|deposit|bill (custom ceremony $600). The sibling's planner words (stages, retainers, month-of billing, the planning consult) are gone with the facts that carried them. Extra time on the day is paid at the visit or on the bill (D91).
